
### 2. ⭐ One reading this seat took that the card did NOT state precisely — and it changes the fence

The card says 「the renderer reads `item.body` through an `any` cast, so the default draws」. The actual line is:

```tsx
 :67  {renderChildren(item.content || (item as any).body)}
```

⇒ the renderer reads **`content` FIRST** and falls back to `body` through the cast. Two consequences, and both belong in the dispatch:

- **respelling the three defaults `body:` → `content:` changes no rendered output** — they move from the fallback arm onto the primary one, and the same nodes render. So the fix is verifiable as a **non**-change at the UI and a change at the parse;
- ⚠️ **the `|| (item as any).body` fallback is a separate, live tolerance** — an undeclared key the renderer still honours. Removing it would be a behaviour removal and it is the `body`-dialect family's question (objectui#9871 and objectui#9910, both in the decision box). ⛔ Out of this card's face, and the dispatch says so.

⛔ **Not objectui#9942** (the vscode extension's `HoverProvider` teaching a `body` sub-list). Same family, different carrier, different defect.

### 4. The deliverable

Respell the three default items so they satisfy `TabItemSchema`. ⭐ Then ask the question that makes this more than a three-line patch: **what stops it coming back?** A default that drifts from its own schema is a class, not an incident, and the repo's own habit is to pin the relation rather than the literal. If a pin can feed `defaultProps.items` through `TabItemSchema` and assert it parses, write it — that is the deliverable's real content. If the registration's shape makes that impossible to reach from a test, say so with the reading and pin what you can.

### 5. Tests

⭐ Assert the **relation**, ⛔ not the literal. A test that checks the three items spell `content` is satisfied forever by a copy-paste; a test that parses them through the published schema fails the day anyone re-spells one.

Controls in the same body, or it is not a reading:
- subject — `defaultProps.items` parses green against `TabItemSchema`;
- control A (the instrument must be able to FAIL) — feed the **old** `body`-spelled item to the same parse and show it is refused, naming `content`;
- control B (the UI must not move) — the rendered output of the default tabs is unchanged, so the respelling is provably a parse-level fix and not a visual one.

### 6. Declared file face

```

```

⛔ Anything outside it is a stop-and-report, ⛔ never a rider. **[SEAT-MEASURED]** `git log` on `tabs.tsx` shows one commit since the card was filed (`f73521f93`, an unrelated docblock dating), and no open PR touches it.

### 7. Stop conditions — a stop with evidence is a good outcome

- Respelling to `content` changes rendered output ⇒ stop and report; §2's reading would then be wrong and that matters more than the patch.
- The only way you can see to pin the relation needs the `body` fallback removed ⇒ stop; that is objectui#9871's, not yours.
- The defaults already parse green on your base ⇒ stop, report what landed and when.

### 8. Deliverable

Branch, code, tests, changeset, push, **draft** PR with `Fixes #9941`. ⛔ Do not flip out of draft, ⛔ do not enqueue, ⛔ do not merge — landing is this seat's act after review. Run the repo's fast checks before pushing. Report back as structured JSON.

## Seat review — ACCEPT. ⭐ The strongest test file of this round, and the reason is the block that runs BEFORE the subject.

Seat `domain:ui#2`, `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`, 2026-09-19T02:41Z. Dev report `status: "done"`, `open_questions: []`. PR objectui#9988: `tabs.tsx` +3/−3, one new pin, one changeset — ⛔ exactly the declared face.

### 1. The change

```diff
-  { label: 'Tab 1', value: 'tab1', body: [{ type: 'text', content: 'Content for Tab 1' }] },
+  { label: 'Tab 1', value: 'tab1', content: [{ type: 'text', content: 'Content for Tab 1' }] },
```
…and the same for items 2 and 3. `TabItemSchema` ⛔ untouched. The `renderChildren(item.content || (item as any).body)` fallback at `:67` ⛔ untouched. Both fences held.

### 2. ⭐ What makes the pin worth more than the three-line patch

**The anti-vacuity block runs first, and it is its own `describe`** — 「the seed is really there — ⛔ a parse over nothing is vacuously green」. It asserts the registration resolves and `items` is a non-empty array **before** any parse runs, with the failure message 「ui:tabs is not registered — every row below is vacuous」. ⇒ this pin cannot pass by finding nothing. That is the single commonest way a parse pin dies quietly, and it is closed here by construction.

**controlA derives the old spelling from the LIVE seed.** `preFix(seededItems())` transforms whatever the registration currently holds, ⛔ it does not re-type the 2026 literal. So the failing control keeps measuring the real seed as the seed changes, and the assertion checks the refusal's **shape** — `code`, `path`, and `expected: 'nonoptional'` — ⛔ not a message string.

**`undeclaredBodyIsDropped` pins a fact the card's prose glossed.** `TabItemSchema.parse({… body: …})` yields keys `['content','label','value']` and ⛔ no `body`: the face **strips** the undeclared key rather than rejecting it. ⇒ the refusal an author sees names the **missing** `content`, ⛔ never the `body` they actually wrote — which is precisely why this defect is loud and undiagnosable at the same time, exactly as triage graded it.

**⭐ controlB has the trap closed.** It asserts `before.text === after.text` **and** `before.html === after.html` across two renders — and then, because two **empty** renders are also equal, adds a lit control that the rendered output actually contains `'Content for Tab 1'`. Without that last line the equality would have passed on a blank screen. This is the reading the dispatch asked for — a change at the **parse** and a provable non-change at the **UI** — and it is the leg most implementations would have shipped broken.

⭐ And the subject's failure message names the wrong fix in advance: 「widening `TabItemSchema`, which would grow an already-published accept set and …」. The fence lives inside the assertion, where the next author will actually meet it.

### 3. The ablation

Run from the COMMITTED state, anchored replace (anchor required to match exactly once per item, ⛔ not `sed -i`), with on-disk proof in **both** directions: injected `body:` items = 3 (want 3), remaining `content:` items = 0 (want 0), mutated blob `502350f2…` ≠ HEAD `cfa19819…`, and the fallback arm still present = 1. Result `Tests 3 failed | 6 passed (9)`, the three reds being exactly the three subject rows. Restore proved by **state** — blob back to `cfa19819…` and an empty `git diff HEAD` — ⛔ not by a trap's exit code.

⚠️ The six controls stayed green in both worlds, and that is **correct, not a defect**: the repair is parse-level, so the controls are pinning a non-change. The dev said so rather than letting it read as weak coverage.

### 4. Two findings from the report, both judged and both acted on

- **To file, class (a) — and this seat re-measured it at source and found it worse than reported.** `content/docs/guide/schema-rendering.md:340`–`:353`'s Lazy Loading fence authors a `tabs` node in which **four** keys are undeclared: `tabs` (declared: `items`), `title` (declared: `label`), `body` (declared: `content`, required), and `lazyLoad`. ⭐ `lazyLoad` is ⛔ not invented — it is real, on `packages/react/src/hooks/usePerformance.ts:44/:90/:165`, as a member of a **performance-hook config**, ⛔ not of any schema node. A key borrowed from another surface is worse than a fabricated one: a reader who searches the repo finds it and concludes their node is right. Filed as **objectui#9989**, with the prose claim 「Large schemas are automatically optimized」 flagged as unmeasured and named as the thing its taker must settle first. ⚠️ `content/docs/**` is the `domain:devx` family under the lane table, so ⛔ routing is not automatic to this lane.
- **Noted, ⛔ not filed, and correctly so**: `examples/schema-catalog/.../basic-tabs.json` already spelled `items[].content`. ⇒ the catalog and the schema agreed and the shipped seed was the lone dissenter, which is why no downstream fixture had to move. Nothing to repair.
